name: Rhythm Path
description: Solves the level, then shows its inputs as a scrolling rhythm-game chart.

show-level-menu.name: Show the menu when opening a level
show-level-menu.description: When you open a level, show the Rhythm Path menu: play a saved chart, import one, or solve the level. The level waits until you choose.

auto-solve.name: Auto-solve when the menu is off
auto-solve.description: Only used when the level menu is turned off: solve automatically if the level has no saved chart.

time-limit.name: Time limit (seconds)
time-limit.description: Time allowed for finding a path in one go. Progress is saved, so you can resume later with more time. Cleaning up and centering the inputs afterwards can take up to 3/4 of this time again, plus a final replay.

solver-fps.name: Solving screen frame rate
solver-fps.description: How smooth the solving screen is. The solver works between frames, so a lower frame rate gives it slightly more time; 60 keeps the game responsive.

ship-wave-precision.name: Ship/wave search precision
ship-wave-precision.description: How closely the solver compares ship, wave, UFO and swing positions. Fast treats nearly identical positions as the same, which stops the search from getting stuck on long ship sections. If a section can't be solved this way, the solver automatically switches to a more exact comparison for that section.

steps-per-update.name: Physics steps per simulated frame
steps-per-update.description: How many 240 TPS physics steps the solver runs per simulated game frame. 4 matches playing at 60 FPS, 1 matches 240 FPS. The final check uses the same value.

input-resolution.name: Input resolution (ticks)
input-resolution.description: The solver may only change an input every N physics ticks (240 per second) while searching. 1 finds the most solutions; 2-4 search faster.

optimize-inputs.name: Clean up the inputs
optimize-inputs.description: After a path is found, remove clicks that aren't needed and shorten taps to the length that actually matters, so the chart has as few notes as possible.

prefer-holds.name: Prefer holding over repeated clicks
prefer-holds.description: When holding the button through a section plays exactly the same as clicking repeatedly (for example a cube jumping on every landing), use one hold note instead.

merge-gap-ms.name: Join ship/wave inputs closer than (ms)
merge-gap-ms.description: While cleaning up, try to join two ship or wave holds separated by a gap shorter than this into one hold, if the level still plays the same.

refine-timing.name: Center inputs in their timing window
refine-timing.description: After a path is found, move every press and release to the middle of the range of ticks that still works, so the chart is as forgiving as possible.

refine-window.name: Centering search range (ticks)
refine-window.description: How far (in 240 TPS ticks) each input is shifted each way while looking for its safe window.

repair-imports.name: Fix imported inputs that fail
repair-imports.description: If imported inputs die before the end, keep the part that works and let the solver find the rest.

section-timing.name: Human-playable timing
section-timing.description: Minimum lengths the solver uses for holds and gaps, so charts stay playable by hand. If a section is impossible with these limits, the solver relaxes them for that section (when allowed below).

other-min-hold-ms.name: Other modes: shortest hold (ms)
other-min-hold-ms.description: Cube, ball, UFO, robot, spider and swing.

other-min-release-ms.name: Other modes: shortest gap between clicks (ms)
other-min-release-ms.description: Cube, ball, UFO, robot, spider and swing.

relax-timing-if-stuck.name: Relax these limits when a section needs it

range-from.name: Show the chart from (%)
range-from.description: Default for every level. You can set a different range for one level in its Rhythm Path menu.

theme.name: Theme
theme.description: Color preset for the chart. Turn on custom colors below to pick your own.

lane-color.name: Lane background
lane-color.description: The alpha value sets how see-through the lanes are.

show-receptors.name: Show key markers on the timing line
show-receptors.description: Markers on the timing line that light up while you hold the button.

orientation.name: Orientation
orientation.description: Horizontal: notes scroll sideways into a vertical timing line. Vertical: notes fall down columns into a horizontal timing line, like FNF.

overlay-position.name: Position
overlay-position.description: Left and Right are for the vertical layout.

custom-x.name: Custom position X
custom-x.description: Center of the chart as a fraction of the screen width (Position: Custom).

custom-y.name: Custom position Y
custom-y.description: Center of the chart as a fraction of the screen height (Position: Custom).

overlay-width.name: Length (fraction of screen)
overlay-width.description: How long the lanes are, along the scroll direction.

hit-line-x.name: Timing line distance from the start of the lanes

scroll-speed.name: Scroll speed
scroll-speed.description: How fast the notes move toward the timing line, in screen units per second of level time.

reverse-scroll.name: Reverse scroll direction
reverse-scroll.description: Horizontal: notes come from the left. Vertical: notes rise from the bottom.

always-show-p2.name: Always show the P2 lane
always-show-p2.description: Show the P2 lane even on levels that are not 2-player.

overlay-opacity.name: Lane opacity
overlay-opacity.description: Multiplies the lane background's own alpha.

idle-fade.name: Fade out when no notes are coming

show-judgements.name: Show hit timing feedback
show-judgements.description: Show how early or late each press and release was.

judge-holds.name: Judge holds
judge-holds.description: Hold notes count as dropped if you let go well before the end.

miss-ms.name: Latest counted hit (ms)
miss-ms.description: Presses further than this from any note are ignored, and notes not hit within it count as a miss.

visual-offset-ms.name: Visual offset (ms)
visual-offset-ms.description: Leave at 0 for exact game-synced timing. Positive values make notes arrive earlier (compensates for display lag).
